system.summary: Book cipher on the book itself: number n at position k gives the initial of the first word beginning with the needed letter, found as word n of physical page k of The Jewel (1652).
system.notes: System is for the octastich; the distich's construction is not established.

prior_solution.where: Vals AI, 31 Aug 2026, same rule and plaintext for the octastich; distich claim also published

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: first-occurrence test with shuffled and random-page controls

solution.what: Provenance objection checked on the 1653 scan and Wilcock 1899.
Octastich measured on Schmeh's 272 numbers and called a book cipher by shape; judged unattackable without the key text.
The poem names its key text (Exskybalauron): number k indexes a word on physical page k of The Jewel.
DP alignment of Schmeh's defective 272 numbers against TCP pages.
Straight decode one number per physical page: 238/284 first-occurrence hits.
Shuffled numbers and random page orders give 0.43 (max 0.51).
Distich Proquiritation rule: 34/64 hits, chance, no English; page-index variants also at chance.

outcome.method_basis: The octastich is a book cipher on The Jewel (1652) itself: word n on physical page k, first word with the needed initial. Vals AI published this rule and plaintext on 31 Aug 2026, before this attempt, and the project verified it against the EEBO-TCP text using a fresh transcription of the numbers.

gaps.detail: TCP text of pp. 149-158 differs from the print (near-empty p. 158); needs the 1652 leaves
claimed Proquiritation rule gives 34/64, chance; page-index variants on The Jewel and Logopandecteision at chance; key text not identified

outcome.notes: Octastich read except ten letters of line 5 (TCP defect at pp. 149-158); distich (64 numbers) unread. Fraction = 275 of 349 numbers across both.
